Know what to ask about your water.

A useful water conversation begins with your home, your source, and your concerns. Ask about a free, no-obligation in-home consultation and water test.

Schedule a Water Consultation

Bring your water story.

Tell the consultant whether your water comes from a utility or private well. If you are unsure, a recent water bill or property information may help. For utility water, bring your Consumer Confidence Report if available; for a well, bring any recent laboratory reports.

Describe what you notice, when it happens, and whether it affects one fixture or several. Photos of spots or buildup can be useful discussion material. Appearance, taste, and smell alone cannot establish water safety.

Ask what the test can tell you.

Florida Pure Solutions’ official site currently advertises a free in-home consultation and water test. Confirm local coverage, appointment availability, and exactly what that test includes before arranging a visit.

An in-home demonstration or screening is not automatically a comprehensive laboratory analysis. Ask which parameters are checked, how results are recorded, and whether your particular concern needs additional testing through an appropriate laboratory.

Turn findings into a practical next step.

Review the results before comparing equipment. Ask how a proposed treatment relates to the specific finding, what a particular model is certified to reduce, and how it should be maintained.

If an urgent safety concern or an official drinking-water advisory applies, follow the relevant utility or public-health guidance. This website and its planner do not determine whether water is safe to drink.

Three questions to bring along.

  1. What does the free in-home test include and exclude?
  2. Do my source water or specific concerns call for additional laboratory testing?
  3. How do the results support the proposed treatment and maintenance plan?

The Water Consultation Planner gives you an ungated checklist you can download before sharing any contact details.
